response.passage: Exercise is essential for a healthy body, but many people have questions about how it works. One common query is whether you need expensive gym equipment to build strength. The truth is that using your own body weight, such as doing push-ups or squats, is an excellent way to build muscle. Another question is when muscles actually grow. Many think muscles grow while you are lifting weights, but they actually grow during the rest periods after exercise when the body repairs tiny tears in the muscle fibers. Regarding fat loss, some believe that sweating is the same as burning fat. In reality, sweating is simply the body’s way of cooling down, not a direct measure of fat loss. Finally, some people worry that warming up is a waste of time. This is incorrect because warming up gradually increases your heart rate and prepares your muscles for activity, which helps prevent injuries. It is also important to keep moving gently after a workout rather than sitting down immediately, as this helps your body recover properly. Always remember that exercise is about consistency and listening to your body, not just about how much you sweat or how heavy the weights are.
response.summary: Exercise helps the body through muscle repair and proper preparation. It is important to understand that sweating and muscle growth work differently than many people assume.
